questions.questionText: In graph theory, which statement correctly defines a spanning tree of a connected undirected graph?
options: A subgraph that includes a subset of vertices and may contain cycles
A subgraph that includes all vertices but must contain at least one cycle
A subgraph that includes all vertices of the original graph and contains no cycles
A subgraph that includes all edges of the original graph regardless of cycles
questions.correctAnswer: A subgraph that includes all vertices of the original graph and contains no cycles
questions.explanation: A spanning tree connects every vertex in the original graph with the minimum number of edges (|V|-1) and, by definition, contains no cycles, making it a tree that spans all vertices.
